items.title: Section: Teaching Correctly Matched to Capacity, Then Gradual Taming Through Three Miraculous Displays — Expanding or Compressing the Teaching as the Listener Actually Needs

items.zh: 愛敬生已，於法起樂；然後為其宣說正法。所說正法，如其所宜，易入易解，應時漸次，無有顛倒，能引義利，堪任難擊。於彼有情調伏事中，成就最勝欲作饒益哀愍之心，為現神通、記心、顯說如理正法。或勸請他，或為化作種種眾多殊特化事，令彼有情皆悉調伏。若引義利極略諸論，能為廣辯；若引義利極廣諸論，能為略說，令其受持。為作憶念，施其問難。彼既於法能受能持，復進為其廣開正義。
items.en: Once affection and respect have arisen, delight in the teaching follows; only then does a bodhisattva actually teach the true dharma. The true dharma thus taught is suited to the occasion, easy to enter and understand, correctly timed and sequenced, undistorted, capable of bringing genuine benefit, and able to withstand even difficult challenge. In the work of taming such beings, bodhisattvas, accomplishing the most excellent wish to benefit and a heart of genuine sympathy, manifest supernormal powers, read minds, and reveal correct teaching accordingly — or entreat another to do so, or conjure many kinds of extraordinary manifestation — so that these beings are entirely tamed. Where a brief teaching, though bringing genuine benefit, is stated too tersely, bodhisattvas expand it into full explanation; where an elaborate teaching, though bringing genuine benefit, is stated too extensively, bodhisattvas compress it so it can actually be retained. They pose questions to aid memory and offer challenges to sharpen understanding. Once such beings are genuinely able to receive and retain the teaching, bodhisattvas proceed further still, opening its correct meaning to them in full.

items.title: Section: Matching Meditation to Affliction, and the Crisis of Faith Sparked by "All Dharmas Are Without Nature" — Why Some Mistake the Perfection of Wisdom for Something Other Than the Buddha's Own Word

items.zh: 又於趣入遍緣一切三摩地門，能為隨順教授教誡，攝益有情令修利行。若諸有情，於佛所說甚深空性相應經典，不解如來密意義趣。於此經中，說一切法皆無自性、皆無有事、無生無滅，說一切法皆等虛空、皆如幻夢。彼聞是已，如其義趣不能解了，心生驚怖，誹謗如是一切經典，言非佛說。菩薩為彼諸有情類，方便善巧如理會通，如是經中如來密意甚深義趣，如實和會，攝彼有情。
items.en: Furthermore, regarding entry into the entire range of meditative absorptions, bodhisattvas offer teaching and admonishment suited to each being, gathering them in and benefiting them so that they cultivate genuinely helpful conduct. Should beings, upon encountering the Buddha's own scriptures joined with profound emptiness, fail to understand the Tathāgata's own hidden intent — scriptures which state that all phenomena are without inherent nature, without real substance, without arising, without ceasing, and that all phenomena are equal to empty space and like illusion and dream — and, upon hearing this, being unable to grasp its intended meaning, become fearful and denounce all such scriptures as not being the Buddha's own word, bodhisattvas, for the sake of these beings, skilfully and correctly reconcile the Tathāgata's own hidden, profound intent within these very scriptures, genuinely harmonising it so as to gather these beings in.

items.title: Section: Reconciling the Crisis Begins — "All Phenomena Are Without Inherent Nature" Never Meant That Nothing Exists at All

items.zh: 菩薩如是正會通時，為彼說言：此經不說一切諸法都無所有，但說諸法所言自性都無所有。是故說言一切諸法皆無自性。
items.en: When bodhisattvas thus correctly reconcile this crisis, they explain to such beings: this sutra does not teach that all phenomena do not exist at all; it teaches only that the verbally-labelled nature of phenomena does not exist. This is why it is said that all phenomena are without inherent nature.

items.title: Section: "No Real Substance" and "No Arising, No Ceasing" — Two Further Resolutions, Each Denying Only the Verbal Label, Never the Underlying Process

items.zh: 雖有一切所言說事，依止彼故諸言說轉，然彼所說可說自性，據第一義非其自性。是故說言一切諸法皆無有事。一切諸法所言自性，理既如是從本已來都無所有，當何所生、當何所滅。是故說言一切諸法無生無滅。
items.en: Although the dependently arisen basis for every verbal statement genuinely exists, and it is by relying on that basis that verbal statements actually proceed, still, the very essence that such statements purport to name, examined according to ultimate truth, is not itself their real essence. This is why it is said that all phenomena have no real substance. Since the verbally-labelled essence of all phenomena, being of this nature, has never existed at all from the very beginning, what could possibly arise, and what could possibly cease? This is why it is said that all phenomena neither arise nor cease.

items.title: Section: Like Space Itself — Colours and Movements Fill Emptiness, and Once They Are Removed, Its Own Purity Shows

items.zh: 譬如空中有眾多色、色業可得，容受一切諸色、色業。謂虛空中，現有種種若往、若來、若住，起墮屈伸等事。若於爾時，諸色、色業皆悉除遣；即於爾時，唯無色性清淨虛空其相顯現。如是即於相似虛空離言說事，有其種種言說所作邪想分別隨戲論著，似色業轉。又即如是一切言說邪想分別隨戲論著似眾色業，皆是似空離言說事之所容受。
items.en: For example, within space, many kinds of form and the activity of form can be found, space accommodating every kind of form and its activity — within space there presently appear various comings, goings, restings, risings, fallings, bendings, and stretchings. Should all such forms and their activity at some point be entirely removed, at that very time, only the pure, colourless nature of space itself would appear. In just this way, within this reality beyond words that resembles space, various mistaken discriminations and conceptual elaborations produced by verbal speech occur, resembling the activity of form. And all such mistaken discriminations and conceptual elaborations resembling the activity of countless forms are themselves accommodated by this reality beyond words that resembles empty space.

items.title: Section: The Noble Mind Realises Space's Own Purity — Yet Never Goes Hunting for Some Further "Thing Called Emptiness" Once the Search Is Done

items.zh: 若時菩薩以妙聖智，遣除一切言說所起邪想分別隨戲論著；爾時菩薩最勝聖者，以妙聖智證得諸法離言說事，唯有一切言說自性非性所顯，譬如虛空清淨相現。亦非過此有餘自性應更尋求。是故宣說一切諸法皆等虛空。
items.en: Once bodhisattvas, through wondrous noble wisdom, dispel every mistaken discrimination and conceptual elaboration arising from verbal speech, at that very time, such supreme, noble bodhisattvas, through this wondrous noble wisdom, realise phenomena's own reality beyond words — a reality disclosing only that every verbally-labelled essence has no corresponding nature, exactly as space's own pure aspect appears. Nor is there, beyond this, some further essence still to be sought. This is why it is proclaimed that all phenomena are equal to empty space.

items.title: Section: Like Illusion and Dream — the Wild Fox Kōan, and Why Denying Karma Outright Is Exactly as Mistaken as Grasping It as Ultimately Real

items.zh: 又如幻夢，非如顯現如實是有，亦非一切幻夢形質都無所有。如是諸法，非如愚夫言說串習勢力所現如實是有，亦非一切諸法勝義離言自性都無所有。
items.en: Furthermore, just as an illusion or a dream should not be taken as genuinely real simply because it vividly appears, neither should the very form and substance of that illusion or dream be taken as utterly nonexistent. In just this way, phenomena should not be taken as genuinely real merely as they are presented through an unlearned person's own habituated force of verbal speech, nor should the ultimate, wordless essence of all phenomena be taken as utterly nonexistent.

items.title: Section: The Reconciliation Closes — Genuine Knowledge That Neither Grasps Nor Abandons a Single Fraction of Reality, Neither Exaggerating Nor Denying

items.zh: 由此方便悟入道理，一切諸法非有非無，猶如幻夢，其性無二。是故宣說一切諸法皆如幻夢。如是菩薩，普於一切諸法法界不取少分、不捨少分、不作損減、不作增益、無所失壞。若法實有，知為實有；若法實無，知為實無；如其所知，如是開示。當知是名菩薩隨順會通方便善巧。
items.en: Through this skilful means, one enters correctly into the understanding that all phenomena are neither existent nor nonexistent, exactly like illusion and dream, their nature undivided. This is why it is proclaimed that all phenomena are like illusion and dream. In this way, bodhisattvas, throughout all phenomena and the dharma-realm, neither grasp the smallest fraction of it, nor abandon the smallest fraction of it; they neither exaggerate what does not exist, nor deny what does exist; nothing is thereby damaged or lost. What is genuinely existent they know as genuinely existent; what is genuinely nonexistent they know as genuinely nonexistent; and, exactly as they know it, so do they teach it. One should understand this to be called a bodhisattva's skilful means of accommodation and reconciliation.

blocks.text: Some beings are frightened when they hear that "all phenomena are without inherent nature". Today the treatise reconciles this teaching: what is denied is the verbal label, never the process.

The teaching should be "suited to the occasion, easy to enter and understand, timely and sequenced, undistorted, beneficial". Master Cháng Bǎi: brief treatises can be expanded, long ones condensed; the bodhisattva is free in both.
Master Cháng Bǎi: for śrāvakas, hearing of emptiness is like a knife cutting the heart; they cannot bear to hear it.

"This sūtra does not teach that all phenomena do not exist at all; only that the verbally-labelled nature of phenomena does not exist." Master Cháng Bǎi: in the word "flower" there is nothing, but the dependently arisen flower the word relies on exists.
"Since the verbally-labelled essence of all phenomena has never existed from the beginning, what could arise and what could cease?"

Master Cháng Bǎi: the mind is originally pure, its true aspect beyond words, but this wordless nature is stained by discrimination and elaboration. Venerable Miào Jìng: this passage briefly explains how birth and death arise. (Note: Ru-Yi's English "never staining" says the opposite of the Chinese here.)
Master Cháng Bǎi: don't cling to a real thing called emptiness. "Not a single thing is found" just means the defiled aspects are gone.

Venerable Miào Jìng: "like space" refers to suchness, the perfected nature; "like illusion and dream" to the dependent nature. The dream events exist, just not truly. Master Cháng Bǎi: illusory appearances are not nothing; one should "not obscure cause and effect", not claim to escape it. "Phenomena are not genuinely real as presented by fools' habituated force of speech, nor is the ultimate, wordless essence of things nonexistent."

"One enters the understanding that all phenomena are neither existent nor nonexistent, like illusion and dream." Venerable Miào Jìng: the imagined nature is utterly empty yet appears; that is inversion.

This is the Yogācāra reading of the Perfection of Wisdom, and it echoes the chapter on reality in fascicle 36. Emptiness removes the label we add, never the world itself. Taking emptiness as "nothing exists" is the error of denial.

quiz.q: What qualities does the treatise say the bodhisattva's teaching has?
options: suited, easy to enter, timely and sequenced, undistorted, beneficial, able to withstand challenge
quiz.why: "Suited to the occasion, easy to enter and understand, timely and sequenced, undistorted, beneficial, able to withstand difficult challenge." Master Cháng Bǎi: the wording is orderly and sequenced, with nothing obscure hidden.

quiz.q: Why do some beings slander scriptures teaching that all phenomena lack nature? How does Master Cháng Bǎi describe the śrāvakas' reaction?
options: śrāvakas hear emptiness like a knife in the heart — they cannot bear hearing that nirvāṇa too is empty
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: for śrāvakas, hearing emptiness is like a knife cutting the heart — they cannot bear to hear that nirvāṇa too is empty. Venerable Miào Jìng: then all the time spent guiding them comes to nothing.

quiz.q: Reconciling for those who slander the emptiness scriptures, what does the bodhisattva say "all phenomena lack nature" means?
options: not that phenomena don't exist, only that their verbally-labelled nature doesn't
quiz.why: "This sūtra does not teach that all phenomena do not exist at all; only that the verbally-labelled nature of phenomena does not exist." Venerable Miào Jìng: note well — it does not say phenomena don't exist. Master Cháng Bǎi: it does not mean even dependently arisen things are absent.

quiz.q: How does the treatise explain "all phenomena neither arise nor cease"?
options: the verbally-labelled nature never existed from the start — what could arise or cease?
quiz.why: "Since the verbally-labelled essence of all phenomena has never existed from the beginning, what could arise and what could cease?" Venerable Miào Jìng: if I don't think it, the lotus isn't there — it never arose at all. Master Cháng Bǎi: before the words were spoken there was no such object, and after, there still isn't.

quiz.q: Phenomena are not real as presented by habituated speech — and also not what?
options: nor is their ultimate, wordless essence wholly nonexistent
quiz.why: "Phenomena are not genuinely real as presented by fools' habituated force of speech, nor is the ultimate, wordless essence of all phenomena wholly nonexistent." Venerable Miào Jìng: since beginningless time beings have had speech.

quiz.q: Through this skilful means, what does one come to understand?
options: all phenomena are neither existent nor nonexistent, like illusion and dream, their nature undivided
quiz.why: "One enters the understanding that all phenomena are neither existent nor nonexistent, like illusion and dream, their nature undivided." Venerable Miào Jìng: realising phenomena are ultimately empty, yet not empty. Master Cháng Bǎi: like illusion and dream — grasping neither existence nor emptiness.
